column8: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3 (NCT05026866, 2,996 participants) enrols people with neither dementia nor mild cognitive impairment: the registry (clinicaltrials.gov API v2, eligibilityModule, checked 2026-11-09) gives ages 55 to 80, requires 'a Telephone Interview for Cognitive Status - modified (TICS-M) score reflective of intact cognitive functioning' and 'a phosphorylated tau (P-tau) result consistent with the presence of amyloid pathology', and excludes mild cognitive impairment. The primary endpoint is time to clinical progression in participants whose baseline Clinical Dementia Rating is 0. Kisunla's label is the mild cognitive impairment and mild dementia stage, so none of this population is in it, and the registry indexes the study under Alzheimer Disease, the same descriptor the symptomatic studies get. The second preclinical study, NCT07571161, enrols in China and is not named here because the book models the US.

column4: Cystic fibrosis without CFTR modulator benefit
column8: ARCT-032 is not for cystic fibrosis. It is for the part of it the modulators cannot reach, and Arcturus says so in its own filing: 'Other treatments are required to target Class I mutations (no CFTR produced; approximately 10% of CF cases worldwide), and people who are intolerant or have poor response to CFTR modulator therapies. We are initially focusing ARCT-032 on these groups of patients' (FY2025 10-K 0001193125-26-088391). The Phase 2 NCT06747858 enrols 'CF adults who do not benefit from current CFTR modulators, including those with Class I null mutations' (Q3 2026 10-Q 0001193125-26-449901). MeSH has no descriptor for the group, so the registry files the study under Cystic Fibrosis (D003550), the same term Trikafta and Alyftrek are indexed under. Separating it is not a refinement: the book holds one prevalence per disease and the two models mean different things by the word. vrtx_trikafta.csv carries prevalence 701 equal to incidence, which is the line-of-therapy convention for a franchise already treating everyone prevalent, so its pool is each year's birth cohort. ARCT-032 has treated nobody, so its pool at launch is the prevalent population that modulators do not serve. Both are right about their own product and they cannot share a row.

Pompe disease is one MeSH descriptor, Glycogen Storage Disease Type II (D006009), and the label splits it where MeSH does not. POMBILITI is indicated 'in combination with miglustat for the treatment of adult patients with late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD)', so the infantile-onset form is outside it. NCT04808505 is filed under the single condition 'Glycogen Storage Disease Type II Infantile Onset' and its official title reads 'in Both ERT-experienced and ERT-naive Pediatric Subjects With Infantile-onset Pompe Disease Aged 0 to < 18 Years'; eligibility requires 'documentation of IOPD genotype' and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy at diagnosis. Its two cohorts are ERT-experienced against ERT-naive within one disease, not two diseases. A row of its own rather than the parent descriptor, or the adult late-onset approval would collapse into it and the readout would read as already decided. Note for whoever prices it: the primary outcome is the proportion of subjects with infusion-associated reactions, a safety endpoint, not efficacy.

column4: BCG-naive high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer
column8: Disjoint on BCG exposure. LABEL (KEYTRUDA, pembrolizumab, openFDA drug/label, set_id 9333c79b-d487-4538-a9f0-71b91a02b287, effective_time 20261016, read 2026-11-14), the only non-muscle-invasive claim in section 1.7: 'KEYTRUDA, as a single agent, is indicated for the treatment of patients with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG)-unresponsive, high-risk, non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS) with or without papillary tumors who are ineligible for or have elected not to undergo cystectomy.' The same section's other bladder claims are locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer and, since the 2026 update, 'in combination with enfortumab vedotin-ejfv, as neoadjuvant treatment and then continued after cystectomy as adjuvant treatment ... with muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC)'; none reaches this study. TRIAL (NCT03711032, KEYNOTE-676, Phase 3, 1,397 participants, clinicaltrials.gov API v2, checked 2026-11-14) is titled for 'High-risk Non-muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer (HR NMIBC) That is Either Persistent or Recurrent Following BCG Induction or That is Naive to BCG Treatment', and the eligibilityModule splits it: Cohort A requires 'Has been treated with one adequate course of BCG induction therapy' and 'Following adequate BCG induction therapy, must have persistent or recurrent HR NMIBC'; Cohort B excludes anyone who 'Has received any prior treatment with BCG for their NMIBC within the past 2 years prior to study entry'. A BCG-naive patient cannot be BCG-unresponsive, and persistence after induction alone is a weaker exposure than the adequate induction-plus-maintenance course that defines BCG-unresponsive disease; neither cohort requires CIS and neither requires cystectomy-ineligibility. The intervention differs too: the label is single-agent pembrolizumab, the study is pembrolizumab plus BCG. MeSH has a Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Neoplasms descriptor (D000093284) but no concept for either BCG-exposure segment, so mesh_id is left empty rather than borrowing the wider one; the registry indexes NCT03711032 only under C565324, Parkinson Disease 4, Autosomal Dominant Lewy Body, which is an indexing error, and data/asset_indication_additions.csv therefore files the study on the asset's Urinary Bladder Neoplasms row (D001749), which is the parent named here.

column4: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer treated with bladder-preserving chemoradiation
column8: Disjoint on the local treatment, and the 2026 label makes the distinction sharper rather than weaker. LABEL (KEYTRUDA, pembrolizumab, openFDA drug/label, set_id 9333c79b-d487-4538-a9f0-71b91a02b287, effective_time 20261016, read 2026-11-14), section 1.7 now carries a muscle-invasive claim: 'KEYTRUDA, in combination with enfortumab vedotin-ejfv, as neoadjuvant treatment and then continued after cystectomy as adjuvant treatment, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC).' Its two other bladder claims are 'locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer' with enfortumab vedotin and 'BCG-unresponsive, high-risk, non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS)'. TRIAL (NCT04241185, KEYNOTE-992, Phase 3, 520 participants, clinicaltrials.gov API v2, checked 2026-11-14): 'A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Clinical Trial to Study the Efficacy and Safety of Pembrolizumab (MK-3475) in Combination With Chemoradiotherapy (CRT) Versus CRT Alone in Participants With Muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer (MIBC)', enrolling patients who 'Has a histologically confirmed initial diagnosis of muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) with predominant urothelial histology', 'Has clinically nonmetastatic bladder cancer (N0M0)' and 'Has planned and is eligible to receive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and one of the protocol-specified radiosensitizing chemotherapy regimens'; primary outcome 'Bladder Intact Event-Free Survival (BI-EFS)'. The label's MIBC indication is defined by the cystectomy it is built around ('continued after cystectomy') and by its partner enfortumab vedotin; KEYNOTE-992 is the bladder-preservation path that exists precisely because the bladder is not removed, with chemoradiation and no enfortumab vedotin. Non-metastatic and muscle-invasive, it is also outside both the NMIBC and the locally advanced/metastatic claims. MeSH has no muscle-invasive descriptor - id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/lookup/term for 'Muscle-Invasive Bladder' returns only the three Non-Muscle Invasive entry terms (checked 2026-11-14) - so mesh_id is empty. The registry files the study under Urinary Bladder Neoplasms (D001749), the parent named here.

Disjoint on line of therapy, at opposite ends of the sequence. LABEL (TUKYSA, tucatinib, openFDA drug/label, set_id f27eb1b9-b7fc-424e-988f-84dd7bb195a3, effective_time 20261014, read 2026-11-14), section 1.2: 'TUKYSA is indicated in combination with trastuzumab for the treatment of adult patients with RAS wild-type, HER2-positive unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer that has progressed following treatment with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy. This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response.' TRIAL (NCT05253651, MOUNTAINEER-03, Phase 3, 400 participants, clinicaltrials.gov API v2, checked 2026-11-14): 'An Open-label Randomized Phase 3 Study of Tucatinib in Combination With Trastuzumab and mFOLFOX6 Versus mFOLFOX6 Given With or Without Either Cetuximab or Bevacizumab as First-line Treatment for Subjects With HER2+ Metastatic Colorectal Cancer', whose first exclusion criterion is 'Prior systemic anticancer therapy for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the locally advanced unresectable or metastatic setting; note that participants may have received a maximum of 2 doses of mFOLFOX6 in the locally advanced/unresectable or metastatic setting prior to randomization.' The label requires progression after three chemotherapy backbones; the study excludes any of them. MeSH has no first-line or HER2-positive colorectal concept (id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/lookup/term for 'First-Line' returns nothing, checked 2026-11-14), so mesh_id is empty and the registry's own descriptor for the study, Colorectal Neoplasms (D015179), is the parent. WHY THE ROW IS NEEDED EVEN THOUGH THE POOL EXISTS. pfe_tukysa.csv already carries this exact population on the Colorectal Neoplasms row at base_pool_overlap_pct 0.0, and the valuation never sees it: TUKYSA's label covers colorectal cancer, so assumptions.load marks the indication approved and forecast._indication_layers skips it, while indication_layer.build would still price the MOUNTAINEER-03 readout off it. The pool rows beside this one move that work onto a row the forecast carries.

Disjoint on both limbs of the indication. LABEL (RASONQUE, daraxonrasib, openFDA drug/label, set_id 13a65923-d072-4dac-8620-8eabbf8c3641, effective_time 20260827, read 2026-11-14), the whole of section 1: 'RASONQUE is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or who are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy.' TRIAL (NCT07491445, RASolute 303, Phase 3, 900 participants, clinicaltrials.gov API v2, checked 2026-11-14): 'RASolute 303: A Phase 3 Global, Multicenter, Open-label, Randomized, 3-Arm Study of Daraxonrasib Monotherapy or Daraxonrasib Plus Gemcitabine and Nab-paclitaxel Versus Gemcitabine and Nab-paclitaxel as a First-Line Treatment for Patients With Metastatic Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma', including 'Diagnosis of metastatic disease <= 6 weeks prior to informed consent' and 'Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1', and excluding 'Prior treatment with systemic anticancer therapy in metastatic setting or prior RAS-targeted therapy in any treatment setting.' No patient has had a prior systemic therapy, so the first limb cannot reach them; and every patient is randomisable to gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel at ECOG 0 to 1, which is what being a candidate for multiagent systemic therapy means, so the second limb cannot either. MeSH has no first-line or metastatic-pancreatic concept (id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/lookup/term for 'Metastatic Pancreatic' returns nothing, checked 2026-11-14), so mesh_id is empty; the registry indexes the study under Pancreatic Neoplasms (D010190), the parent named here and the descriptor the approved second-line layer already sits on. rvmd_rasonque.csv's own base_pool_overlap_pct note asks for exactly this row: 'A human has to decide whether to retire the loaded eligible_pct and re-cut this layer, or carry the first line as a layer of its own.'

column4: Unresectable stage III ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer
column8: Disjoint because the study enrols the gap between the two approved settings. LABEL (ALECENSA, alectinib, openFDA drug/label, set_id 42c49deb-713b-427a-9670-08af08adcffb, effective_time 20260821, read 2026-11-14), both indications in full: 'ALECENSA is indicated as adjuvant treatment in adult patients following tumor resection of anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (tumors >= 4 cm or node positive), as detected by an FDA-approved test' (1.1) and 'ALECENSA is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC as detected by an FDA-approved test' (1.2). TRIAL (NCT05170204, HORIZON 1, Phase 3, clinicaltrials.gov API v2, checked 2026-11-14): 'A Phase I-III, Multicenter Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Multiple Therapies in Cohorts of Patients Selected According to Biomarker Status, With Locally Advanced, Unresectable, Stage III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer', enrolling patients 'Histologically or cytologically documented locally advanced, unresectable Stage III NSCLC of either squamous or non-squamous histology' with 'Prior receipt of at least two prior cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy given cCRT; or at least two prior cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy given prior to radiotherapy (sCRT)' and 'No disease progression during or following platinum-based cCRT or sCRT', excluding 'Any evidence of Stage IV disease' and 'Any history of previous NSCLC and/or any history of prior treatment for NSCLC (participants must be newly diagnosed with unresectable Stage III disease)'; Cohort A1 additionally requires 'Documented ALK fusion positivity' and randomises 'Cohort A1: Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase (ALK)-positive (Alectinib Arm)' against 'Cohort A1: ALK-positive (Durvalumab Arm)'. Unresectable means not resected, so the adjuvant indication cannot reach these patients; the Stage IV exclusion means they are not metastatic, so the second cannot either. The comparator being durvalumab, the approved consolidation after chemoradiation in this setting, confirms which slot it is. MeSH has no staging concept (id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/lookup/term for 'Unresectable' returns nothing and for 'Stage III' returns only a Norwood procedure and a Bacillus protein, checked 2026-11-14), so mesh_id is empty; the registry indexes the study under Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung (D002289), the parent named here.

column4: Ocular complications of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa
column8: Disjoint use in overlapping people, and the label settles it on the route rather than the disease. LABEL (VYJUVEK, beremagene geperpavec-svdt, openFDA drug/label, set_id fe207c8c-04b4-4fdf-87cf-6dbc7eb6e9c2, effective_time 20250929, read 2026-11-14), section 1 in full: 'VYJUVEK is indicated for the treatment of wounds in adult and pediatric patients with dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB) with mutation(s) in the collagen type VII alpha 1 chain (COL7A1) gene', and section 2.2 'For topical application on wounds only. ... Apply VYJUVEK gel to the selected wound(s) in droplets spaced evenly within the wound, approximately 1cm-by-1cm apart.' TRIAL (NCT07016750, IOLITE, Phase 3, 16 participants, clinicaltrials.gov API v2, checked 2026-11-14): 'A Double-Blind Crossover of KB803 and Matched Placebo for the Treatment and Prevention of Corneal Abrasions in Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa', enrolling 'Age 6 months or older at time of informed consent/assent', 'Confirmed diagnosis of DEB with a mutation in the COL7A1 gene' and 'Meets minimum corneal abrasion symptom frequency in the NHS study'. The patients are DEB patients and many are already on VYJUVEK for skin wounds, so the people are not disjoint; the treated manifestation, the route and the product are. KB803 is a redosable eye drop formulation applied to the ocular surface, which the label's 'on wounds only' dosing does not authorise and the gel presentation cannot deliver; Krystal's own FY2025 10-K (0001711279-26-000016) describes it as a separate programme, 'KB803 (Ophthalmic B-VEC) for Ocular Complications of DEB', and reports it as its own segment. It will carry its own approval, its own price and its own dosing, so pricing it at zero on skin-wound overlap omits a product rather than avoiding a double count. MeSH has no DEB-ocular concept: the registry's second descriptor for the study is Corneal Injuries (D065306), which is the injury in anyone, not the DEB subset, and id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/lookup/term returns 'Corneal Abrasions' only as an entry term (checked 2026-11-14), so mesh_id is empty. Parent is D016108, the registry's primary descriptor for the study and the asset's own row.

column4: Symptomatic peripheral arterial disease at body mass index 23 to under 27
column8: Partly disjoint, and the overlap is a band of body mass index rather than a disease. LABEL (FOUNDAYO, orforglipron, openFDA drug/label, set_id 8ac446c5-feba-474f-a103-23facb9b5c62, effective_time 20260729, read 2026-11-14), section 1 in full: 'FOUNDAYO is indicated in combination with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in adults with obesity or adults with overweight in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition', with the numbers given in Clinical Studies: 'enrolled 3,127 adult patients with obesity (BMI >= 30 kg/m2), or with overweight (BMI 27 to <30 kg/m2) and at least one weight-related comorbid condition'. TRIAL (NCT07223593, ATTAIN-PAD, Phase 3, 1,205 participants, clinicaltrials.gov API v2, checked 2026-11-14): 'A Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Orforglipron Once Daily in Participants With Peripheral Artery Disease'. Its complete inclusion criteria are 'Have symptomatic PAD with intermittent claudication of Fontaine Stage II' and 'Have an Ankle Brachial Index (ABI) of 0.9 or less'; the only weight-related criterion anywhere in the record is the exclusion 'Have a body mass index (BMI) less than 23 kilogram per square meter (kg/m2)'. Alone among the ATTAIN comorbidity studies this one carries no obesity or overweight entry requirement, in the title or in the criteria, so it enrols from BMI 23 upwards and the BMI 23 to under 27 band is outside the approved population on both of the label's limbs. The BMI 27 and over remainder is in the base and is left on the Peripheral Arterial Disease row, which lly_foundayo.csv already carries at base_pool_overlap_pct 1.0; this row is the band below it only. MeSH has no body-mass-index subpopulation concept, so mesh_id is empty; the registry indexes the study under Peripheral Arterial Disease (D058729), the parent named here.

Partly disjoint on the HER2 score, and only on the score. LABEL (ENHERTU, fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki, openFDA drug/label, set_id 7e67e73e-ddf4-4e4d-8b50-09d7514910b6, effective_time 20260515, read 2026-11-14), the tumour-agnostic claim that would otherwise cover pancreatic cancer, section 1.6: 'ENHERTU, as monotherapy, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive (IHC 3+) solid tumors who have received prior systemic treatment and have no satisfactory alternative treatment options', approved under accelerated approval. No other section reaches pancreatic adenocarcinoma: 1.1 to 1.3 are breast, 1.4 HER2-mutant NSCLC, 1.5 gastric or gastroesophageal junction. TRIAL (NCT04482309, DESTINY-PanTumor02, Phase 2, 477 participants, clinicaltrials.gov API v2, checked 2026-11-14) enrols 'Locally advanced, unresectable, or metastatic disease', 'Part 1: The respective cohorts for patient inclusion are: ... Cohort 6: Pancreatic cancer', 'Progressed following prior treatment or who have no satisfactory alternative treatment option' and, on the score, 'HER2 expression scored using current ASCO/CAP guidelines ... Part 1: IHC 3+ or IHC 2+ by local or central assessment'; Part 2 Cohort B is 'Metastatic or advanced solid tumors that are HER2 IHC 2+/ISH+ any tumor type (excluding breast, gastric cancer, and colorectal cancer)'. The IHC 3+ pancreatic patients are genuinely inside section 1.6 and azn_enhertu.csv is right to hold them at base_pool_overlap_pct 1.0 on the Pancreatic Neoplasms row. The IHC 2+ patients are reachable under no current ENHERTU indication, and IHC 2+ is the larger share of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. This row is the IHC 2+ slice only, which is the thing most at risk of being over-sized if someone prices the whole cohort. MeSH has no HER2-score concept, so mesh_id is empty; the registry indexes the study under Pancreatic Neoplasms (D010190) and Colorectal Neoplasms (D015179), and D010190 is the parent for the pancreatic cohort.

column4: Advanced chronic kidney disease (eGFR 25 or below, dialysis, or kidney transplant)
column8: RENAL LIFECYCLE (University Medical Center Groningen lead; collaborators AstraZeneca and the Dutch Kidney Foundation; about 1,750 participants; dapagliflozin 10 mg/day against placebo) enrols 'Patients with advanced CKD i.e. an eGFR <=25 mL/min/1.73m2', 'Dialysis patients (at least 3 months after start of dialysis)' and 'Transplant patients with an eGFR <=45 mL/min/1.73m2'. Its primary outcome is the composite of all-cause mortality, kidney failure and hospitalisation for heart failure (registry, clinicaltrials.gov API v2, checked 2026-11-16). The Farxiga label (api.fda.gov set id 72ad22ae-efe6-4cd6-a302-98aaee423d69, effective 2026-06-03) approves CKD at risk of progression. But it says 'Initiation with FARXIGA is not recommended in patients with an eGFR less than 25 mL/min/1.73 m2' and 'Efficacy and safety trials with FARXIGA did not enroll patients with an eGFR less than 25 mL/min/1.73 m2 or on dialysis'. The study therefore enrols the part of CKD the label does not recommend starting in, and an approved-CKD link would read the readout as settled. label_covers is 'no' for initiation. The label lets a patient whose eGFR falls below 25 on treatment continue, so some prevalent users in the pool are already inside the revenue. MeSH has no concept for advanced CKD.
